units.function: Embedded-Postgres and pure policy tests for default-on multi-Project workspace references, local/remote driver classification, Company availability filtering, per-Project read authorization, anchor dedupe and bounded admission/authorization fan-out.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat mention resolution reads Project links from Issue sources, loads Company-scoped Projects, treats the anchor as already authorized by the parent Work path, asks AuthorizationService for project:read on additional candidates, then returns admitted Project records and human-readable warnings to workspace preparation.
units.keyDataModels: Issue anchor and mentioned Project IDs, AuthorizationActor/Decision/project:read, Company boundary, admitted/evaluation caps, warnings, feature kill-switch env and remote driver classification.
units.lifecycle: Cross-Project sync is on unless explicitly disabled; the anchor is removed from mentions and not re-authorized; unavailable/foreign Projects are dropped before authorization, denials or authorization errors are dropped with warnings while the Run continues; only admitted Projects consume the materialization cap, only available candidates consume the evaluation cap, and evaluation fan-out is bounded under mention floods.
units.testAssessment: Fifteen cases cover feature parsing, driver classification, same-Company admission, anchor dedupe, foreign/unavailable filtering, deny/exception fail-closed behavior, admitted/evaluation caps, denied-first and unavailable-first ordering, flood behavior and cap invariants. Missing are authentication of mention authors, Project/file/data classification, anchor authorization proof, authorization decision version/expiry/revocation, mandatory versus optional source semantics, stable structured failures in this resolver, concurrent Project/permission changes, large real Issue sources, query plans, audit receipts and end-to-end workspace content integrity. Mention order can consume the evaluation window with denied candidates and displace a later authorized source.
units.designRationale: Allow Agents to draw on explicitly mentioned same-Company Projects while enforcing read policy and bounding database/authorization/materialization work under malicious or accidental mention floods.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explicit multi-source DataAuthorizationContracts and egress controls so Agents can use approved company knowledge without a mention silently widening their accessible data surface.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT Company prefiltering, per-source authorization, separate evaluation/admission limits, anchor dedupe, fail-closed decisions and structured omission reporting. Make cross-source access opt-in through a versioned Work data contract that identifies required/optional sources, file/query scope, classification, purpose, retention, destination and accountable approver. Snapshot authorization decisions and source digests at dispatch; required-source denial fails the Work, optional denial produces a typed degraded-mode decision. Prevent mention-order starvation with deterministic policy priority or explicit selection rather than first-N text order.
units.responsibilityConflict: A mention plus Agent project:read is sufficient to widen context; no accountable human approves the disclosure or degraded execution. The anchor bypasses this resolver's authorization, overall work continues after denied/error sources, and warnings are not immutable data-access receipts. Default-on behavior is unsuitable for enterprise data boundaries without a Company policy contract.

units.function: Pure policy tests for staging authorized referenced Projects into remote execution targets, with a remote kill switch, confined-transport gate and the same Project/evaluation caps.
units.dependencyDirection: resolveAdditionalRunWorkspaces receives caller-computed remote/confined flags, reads mentions, loads candidates, invokes project:read authorization and a workspace resolver, then supplies staged workspace descriptors to the remote execution preparation path.
units.keyDataModels: Remote sync feature flag, executionTargetIsRemote, targetStagesConfined, sandbox/SSH/plugin driver classification, anchor Project, authorization actor/decision, staged workspace path and structured authorization/resolution/staging failure.
units.lifecycle: Remote sync is on unless explicitly disabled, but only sandbox is classified as confined; a disabled flag or unconfined SSH/plugin target drops every referenced source before authorization/staging; a confined sandbox authorizes and stages allowed non-anchor Projects, drops denied ones, and retains candidate/admission caps.
units.testAssessment: Nine pure cases cover flag parsing, confined driver classification, allowed sandbox staging, disabled fail-closed behavior, SSH exclusion, denial, anchor exemption and both caps. Missing are a real sandbox provider/upload path, cryptographic environment attestation, path confinement and symlink/archive traversal, source snapshot/hash, encryption, upload cancellation/cleanup, egress/retention policy, secret handling, plugin-provided confinement capability, remote data residency, staged file scope and authorization revocation. targetStagesConfined is trusted input; the stub merely returns a local /tmp path, so actual confinement is unproven. Cap overflow is labeled resolution rather than a distinct policy-limit code.
units.designRationale: Permit multi-Project context only when the remote transport claims per-tree confinement, keep a rapid rollback switch and preserve authorization/fan-out limits on the new remote path.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS hybrid deployments need safe, provable staging of authorized data from the control plane or customer node into an execution sandbox, with complete export and deletion evidence.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the transport capability gate, pre-staging authorization, kill switch and bounded fan-out. Replace the Boolean with a signed ExecutionEnvironment attestation declaring filesystem isolation, encryption, region, egress and cleanup guarantees; generate a content-addressed StagingManifest from the DataAuthorizationContract, encrypt to the node, verify receipt/hash, enforce read-only mounts and record deletion/retention evidence. SSH/plugin transports may participate only after satisfying the same contract, not by hardcoded driver names.
units.responsibilityConflict: No accountable human or Company data-export policy approves moving Project contents to the sandbox. The anchor is exempt, sandbox confinement is asserted rather than proven, and denied/staging failures still permit execution without an explicit degraded-mode owner decision. Workspace paths are operational hints, not evidence of what data crossed the boundary.
